correctness.rationale: The allocation state t identifies a complete equivalence class of deterministic preallocations. The independent comparison signs give Q_t=t+Z/2. Conditional on the heavy sign, Z is 2K or 2(K-r), and multiplying independent non-envy tails yields both closed forms, including equality atoms. Direct subtraction yields the single-crossing rule. The exact P1-P0 numerator has sign positive precisely from r=3. Concentration proves t_r/r ->1/2. Standalone exact checker reproduced the distribution independently for 65 cases and compared 200 thresholds; finite computation is corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The theorem classifies exact ex-post EF probabilities and the r=3 threshold for precommitted heterogeneous binary lottery goods. value.rationale: The precommitted allocation model naturally asks whether equalizing expectations also maximizes joint realized no-envy probability. This theorem supplies an exact infinite-family phase boundary and optimizer, not a small ad-hoc example, and identifies discrete atoms and heterogeneous scale as causes of an ex-ante/ex-post discrepancy. The failure starts at three small goods and its optimal split approaches one half; such an exact boundary helps distinguish robust fair preallocations from expectation-balanced ones.
